results.title: Reflected XSS in Search Parameter
results.description: The application reflects user input from the search parameter without proper encoding, allowing execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser.
results.suggested_fix: Encode all user-controlled data in HTML context (e.g. use context-safe encoding). Implement Content-Security-Policy and consider using a template engine that auto-escapes by default.

results.title: SQL Injection in Login Form
results.description: The login form concatenates user input into SQL queries, allowing an attacker to modify query logic and potentially extract or modify database data.
results.suggested_fix: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements for all database access. Never concatenate user input into SQL strings.

results.title: Missing Security Headers
results.description: Responses do not include X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, or Content-Security-Policy, increasing risk of clickjacking and MIME sniffing attacks.
results.suggested_fix: Add security headers: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN, Content-Security-Policy with a restrictive policy.

results.title: Session Cookie Without Secure Flag

compliance_controls.PCI_DSS_6_5_10: PCI DSS - 6.5.10 Broken authentication and session management
compliance_controls.ISO27002_A14_1_3: ISO 27002 - A.14.1.3 Protecting application services transactions

results.description: Session cookie is set without the Secure attribute, allowing transmission over unencrypted HTTP and increasing risk of session hijacking.
results.suggested_fix: Set Secure and HttpOnly on session cookies. Prefer SameSite=Strict or Lax. Use HTTPS only.

results.title: Sensitive Data Exposure in Error Page
results.description: The error page displays stack traces and internal paths to unauthenticated users, which may aid attackers in reconnaissance.
results.suggested_fix: Return generic error messages to users. Log detailed errors server-side only. Disable debug mode in production.
